release_notes_justification:
URL: https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/releases

Release notes are published per tagged GitHub Release and mirrored in per-crate `crates/*/CHANGELOG.md` (Keep a Changelog format, Added / Fixed / Other sections with PR links). Generated by release-plz from Conventional Commits — curated summaries, not raw git log. Each published crate in the Cargo workspace has its own SemVer track and changelog entry per release.
release_notes_vulns_justification: No CVE or GHSA has ever been published against tsoracle. The repository's Security Advisories list (https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/security/advisories) is empty, and no CVE/GHSA identifier appears in any release notes or per-crate `CHANGELOG.md`. Per the criterion text, this case selects N/A. `SECURITY.md` documents the private reporting channel so that when a vulnerability is reported and fixed, future release notes can identify it by CVE/GHSA.
report_responses_justification: Bug reports and feature requests are tracked at https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/issues and responded to by the maintainers. Issues are triaged within days of being filed; the majority are resolved by a merged PR within weeks. The issue tracker is public, supports labeling, and links bidirectionally to commits and PRs.
enhancement_responses_justification: Enhancement requests filed as GitHub Issues are responded to by the maintainers. Where an enhancement is accepted, a tracking issue or PR is opened; where rejected, the rationale is recorded on the issue thread. The issue tracker at https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/issues is the canonical channel.
report_archive_justification:
URL: https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/issues?q=is%3Aissue

GitHub Issues serves as the public, permanent archive of bug reports, feature requests, and discussion. Closed issues remain visible and searchable; every issue has a stable URL. PRs are similarly archived at https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/pulls?q=is%3Apr.
vulnerability_report_process_justificati:
URL: https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/blob/main/SECURITY.md

`SECURITY.md` documents the end-to-end reporting flow: where to file (private draft Security Advisory at https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/security/advisories/new — not public issues), what to include (affected versions, impact, minimal reproduction, severity), response commitments (24h ack, 72h triage, 30d coordinated disclosure or sooner), in/out-of-scope surface, and the post-fix disclosure flow with CVE via the GitHub CNA.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati:
URL: https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/security/advisories/new

The project's SECURITY.md directs reporters to GitHub's private Security Advisories channel, which is encrypted in transit (TLS) and visible only to repository maintainers. SECURITY.md additionally invites reporters to request an out-of-band encrypted channel via a follow-up comment on the advisory if they need stronger pre-disclosure secrecy.
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability reports have been received against tsoracle to date. The project's Security Advisories list (https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/security/advisories) contains zero advisories, draft or published. When a report is received, SECURITY.md commits the project to acknowledgment within 24 hours and triage within 72 hours; the criterion will become demonstrably Met after the first report is responded to within those windows.
build_floss_tools_justification: The build uses cargo and the rustc Rust compiler — both released under the FLOSS dual MIT/Apache-2.0 license (https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/master/COPYRIGHT). Supporting build-time tools enforced by CI (protoc, buf, clang/libclang, cargo-llvm-cov, cargo-deny) are all FLOSS. No proprietary tooling is required to build the project from source.
test_justification: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked` on every push and PR, covering unit tests across the 17 workspace crates and ~30 integration tests under `crates/*/tests/`, plus the failpoint and yieldpoint feature suites (see `docs/failpoint-testing.md`, `docs/yieldpoint-testing.md`). A cross-platform driver-file job runs on Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows. Out-of-process: 15+ libFuzzer harnesses (`fuzz/fuzz_targets/`), the kube-e2e and mixed-version-soak Kubernetes lanes, the stress-smoke PR job (mem/raft/paxos/process topologies with a positive-control inject-violation step), and nightly leak/fuzz/stress workflows.
test_most_justification: Coverage is measured by cargo-llvm-cov in the `coverage` CI job and uploaded to Coveralls (https://coveralls.io/github/prisma-risk/tsoracle). The most recent measurement is approximately 95% line coverage across the workspace, indicating that most major functionality is exercised by automated tests. Critical paths (consensus drivers, timestamp allocator, leader handoff) are covered by dedicated integration test files and additionally by fuzz harnesses for input-decoder paths.
test_policy_justification:
URL: https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#test-policy

`CONTRIBUTING.md` `## Test policy` requires every contribution adding functionality to include automated tests, and every bug fix to include a regression test that fails on the unfixed code and passes on the fix. CI required check runs `cargo test --workspace --all-features`. Exempt: `docs:` / `refactor:` / `chore:` (no runtime behavior change). Backed by ~95% workspace line coverage (cargo-llvm-cov → Coveralls).
tests_are_added_justification:
URL: https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#test-policy

`CONTRIBUTING.md` `## Test policy` requires that every contribution adding new functionality MUST include automated tests, and every bug fix MUST include a regression test that fails on the unfixed code and passes on the fix. Enforced at review time and reinforced by ~95% workspace line coverage (cargo-llvm-cov → Coveralls).
warnings_justification: Compiler warnings (cargo default) plus Clippy lints — the canonical Rust linter — run in CI via `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings` (see `.github/workflows/ci.yml`). `-D warnings` promotes every warning to a hard error. Library and binary crates carry `#![cfg_attr(not(test), warn(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used))]` at the crate root to flag panicking calls in non-test code (documented in `CONTRIBUTING.md`).
warnings_fixed_justification: Because clippy runs with `-D warnings` in CI as a required check, no PR can merge into main with an outstanding warning. The workspace contains no `#![allow]` overrides at the workspace or crate level for lint groups. The pre-commit hook in .husky/pre-commit additionally runs fmt + clippy locally before commit, surfacing warnings before they reach CI.
know_secure_design_justification: At least one project member is familiar with secure design principles, demonstrated by concrete decisions: (1) TLS/mTLS on peer and admin transport, with a Helm chart guard that refuses to render HA openraft/paxos without TLS unless `tls.allowInsecurePeer=true`; (2) fail-closed defaults on the consensus/timestamp critical path (single-active leadership-stream lease, synchronous WatchGuard step-down at the drop site, openraft graceful handoff before drain); (3) defense-in-depth on the client (per-pass + absolute redirect caps); (4) `SECURITY.md` triage / CNA-coordinated CVE disclosure flow; (5) gRPC decode-boundary input validation backed by 15+ libFuzzer harnesses.
know_common_errors_justification: At least one project member is familiar with common vulnerability classes. Safe Rust structurally excludes the memory-safety class (buffer overflow, use-after-free, double-free, `Send`/`Sync` data races). For classes Rust does not prevent: (1) 15+ libFuzzer harnesses (`fuzz/fuzz_targets/`) exercise codec/proto decode paths against malformed input, per-PR and nightly with auto-issue filing on crash; (2) cargo-deny enforces a FLOSS-only license allow-list and the RustSec advisory database; (3) OpenSSF Scorecard runs per push and weekly; (4) Dependabot updates Actions, fuzz workspace, and base image digests; base images SHA256-pinned in `deploy/Dockerfile`.
crypto_published_justification: The project does not implement cryptographic algorithms itself. Where it uses cryptography (TLS for the gRPC client/server and peer transport), it relies on `rustls` via `tonic`, which uses the published `ring` / `aws-lc-rs` providers exercising standardized algorithms documented by IETF RFCs (TLS 1.3 cipher suites, ECDSA, RSA-PKCS#1, X25519, AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305).
crypto_call_justification: The project does not implement cryptography itself and does not expose cryptographic algorithm selection to its users as a tunable surface. Cryptographic choices are delegated to rustls/tonic defaults (modern TLS 1.3 cipher suites). The criterion applies to projects that select among multiple cryptographic algorithms at the application layer; tsoracle does not.
crypto_floss_justification: All cryptographic implementations the project depends on are FLOSS: rustls (Apache-2.0/MIT/ISC), ring (ISC with a mixed-license historical statement), tonic (MIT). The cargo-deny `deny.toml` license allow-list (Apache-2.0, MIT, BSD-3-Clause, ISC, Unicode-3.0, Zlib) is enforced in CI and would reject a non-FLOSS crypto dependency on the next PR.
crypto_keylength_justification: The project uses TLS 1.3 via rustls defaults, which selects key lengths providing at least 128-bit security (X25519 with curve25519 / P-256 / RSA-2048 minimum / AES-128-GCM / AES-256-GCM / ChaCha20-Poly1305). The project does not implement its own crypto with sub-112-bit-security algorithms.
crypto_working_justification: The project uses TLS 1.3 via rustls defaults. The rustls default profile rejects TLS 1.0/1.1 and weak/broken cipher suites (MD5 signature algorithms, RC4, DES/3DES, NULL ciphers, export-grade key exchange). The project does not use known-broken algorithms anywhere in its own source.
crypto_pfs_justification: TLS 1.3 — the only protocol version rustls offers by default for tsoracle's transports — mandates ephemeral Diffie-Hellman key exchange (X25519 / secp256r1 / secp384r1) for every handshake, so perfect forward secrecy is provided for every session.
crypto_password_storage_justification: The project does not authenticate users by password. Authentication between peers and between clients and the server is via mutual TLS (X.509 certificates), not passwords. No user-supplied secret is stored or compared by the project.
crypto_random_justification: The project uses the `rand` crate (workspace pin: rand = { version = '0.9', default-features = false, features = ['std', 'std_rng'] }) where `std_rng` is `ChaCha12Rng`, a cryptographically-secure PRNG, seeded via the `getrandom` crate from the OS CSPRNG (`/dev/urandom`, `getrandom(2)`, `BCryptGenRandom` per platform). For TLS, rustls uses its provider's CSPRNG (ring/aws-lc-rs). The project does not use `thread_rng()` in security-critical paths and does not implement its own PRNG.
delivery_unsigned_justification: Distributed artifacts carry cryptographic integrity protection: (1) crates.io tarballs are referenced by SHA-256 in any consumer's `Cargo.lock`, so transport-level tampering would change the consumer's lockfile; (2) ghcr.io container images are content-addressable by SHA256 digest, and `deploy/Dockerfile` pins base images by digest; (3) GitHub release tags are immutable git refs identified by SHA-1 commit; (4) distribution channels are HTTPS-only (see delivery_mitm).
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No publicly known vulnerability has been disclosed against tsoracle to date — the project's Security Advisories list (https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/security/advisories) contains zero advisories, draft or published, and no CVE has been assigned. Therefore there has been no past instance where the 60-day clock could be either met or missed. The project's SECURITY.md commits to coordinated disclosure within 30 days from report (or sooner on fix release), well inside the 60-day criterion.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No critical vulnerability has been publicly disclosed against tsoracle. SECURITY.md commits the project to coordinated disclosure within 30 days and to requesting a CVE via the GitHub CNA when the impact warrants one.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: A grep of the repository for common secret patterns (BEGIN PRIVATE KEY, BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY, BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY, AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}, ghp_, aws_access_key) across .rs, .toml, .yml, and .md files returns zero matches. The only TLS/PKI material in the repository is test-only certificate generation via the `rcgen` crate at test-fixture time; no static private keys are committed. .gitignore excludes typical credential paths, and OpenSSF Scorecard's pinned-dependencies / token-permissions checks run on every push.
static_analysis_justification: Three static-analysis categories run on every push / PR (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`): (1) Clippy with `--workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings`; (2) cargo-deny enforces a FLOSS-only license allow-list (`deny.toml`) plus the RustSec advisory database; (3) OpenSSF Scorecard (`.github/workflows/scorecard.yml`). Project-specific guards: `scripts/check-critical-path.sh` (no `tracing!` / `println!` / sync-I/O on hot-path files), `scripts/check-ts-header.py` (Apache-2.0 short header).
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Because clippy runs with `-D warnings` (denying every warning to error) and the deny / header-check / critical-path guards are all required CI gates, no PR can merge with an outstanding static-analysis finding. The workspace contains no global `#![allow]` overrides on lint groups.
static_analysis_often_justification: Static analysis runs on every push to main and every pull request (see the `clippy`, `deny`, `header-check`, and `critical-path` jobs in .github/workflows/ci.yml — triggered by `on: push: branches: [main]` and `on: pull_request`). OpenSSF Scorecard runs additionally on a weekly cron (`43 18 * * 6` in .github/workflows/scorecard.yml) and on every main-branch push.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: All medium-or-higher dynamic-analysis findings are fixed and gated on main: (1) libFuzzer per-PR (`fuzz-pr.yml`) and nightly with 30-min/target budget (`fuzz-nightly.yml`), crashes auto-file as issues; (2) `kube-e2e.yml` and `kube-e2e-mixed-version.yml` gate on a 0.05% soak error budget; (3) `stress-smoke` runs mem/raft/paxos/process topologies with a positive-control `inject-violation` step that must exit 1 to prove the supervisor still catches monotonicity breaks; (4) `leak-nightly.yml`. None report unresolved findings on main.
report_tracker_justification: GitHub Issues is the project's issue tracker (https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/issues). It is publicly readable, supports anyone with a GitHub account filing new issues, supports labeling, milestones, assignment, cross-references to commits/PRs, and search across open and closed history.
tests_documented_added_justification: Met via CONTRIBUTING.md's `## Test policy` section (see test_policy at passing tier for the URL and full text), which states new functionality must include tests and bug fixes must include at least one regression test. The policy is documented in the same file that documents the project's other contribution policies (panic policy, license headers, performance-critical-path rules, Conventional Commits).
warnings_strict_justification: The project's CI runs `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings`, treating every warning as a hard error. Library and binary crates additionally carry `#![cfg_attr(not(test), warn(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used))]` to escalate panicking patterns in non-test code. No `#![allow]` overrides are present at the workspace level, and no workarounds (e.g., `clippy.toml allow-unwrap-in-tests`) are used to silence the lint.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: The project does not implement cryptographic algorithms; it consumes rustls via tonic. Rustls maintains its own cipher-suite hygiene upstream — no SHA-1 in signature contexts, no RC4, no DES/3DES, no 64-bit block ciphers, no TLS 1.0/1.1, no insecure curves — and tsoracle inherits those choices via the rustls default ClientConfig/ServerConfig.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: Static analysis aimed at common vulnerability patterns: (1) Clippy lints catch suspicious / panicking patterns (`unwrap_used`, `expect_used`, integer-overflow-prone idioms), with `-D warnings`; (2) cargo-deny enforces the RustSec advisory database against the dependency tree; (3) OpenSSF Scorecard tracks supply-chain patterns; (4) safe Rust structurally excludes the memory-safety vulnerability class.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: Memory-safety dynamic analysis is satisfied structurally by safe Rust, which excludes the buffer-overflow / use-after-free / double-free / `Send`/`Sync` data-race classes at compile time. The few `unsafe` blocks in the workspace are inside vetted third-party deps (e.g. `tokio`, `rustls`); the project's own code has no `unsafe`. cargo-deny in the `deny` CI job tracks the RustSec advisory database against the dependency tree.
dco_justification:
URL: https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#developer-certificate-of-origin

CONTRIBUTING.md's 'Developer Certificate of Origin' section requires every commit to carry a Signed-off-by trailer attesting to DCO v1.1 (https://developercertificate.org/). The DCO GitHub App (https://github.com/apps/dco) is installed as a required PR check; a PR with any unsigned commit fails the check and cannot be merged. DCO is layered on top of the project's Apache-2.0 inbound = outbound licensing under GitHub ToS §D.6.
governance_justification:
URL: https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md

GOVERNANCE.md documents project mission, structure, roles (maintainer, reviewer, contributor), decision-making, the path to becoming a maintainer, and a continuity-of-access plan with named maintainers and a named secondary contact. Documents the lead-maintainer-plus-co-maintainers model (§3.1); with three active maintainers the bus_factor criterion is now met.
code_of_conduct_justification:
URL: https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md

The project adopts the Contributor Covenant v2.1 (https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct/), shipped as CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md at the repository root. CONTRIBUTING.md links to it and to the private reporting channel for code-of-conduct concerns.
roles_responsibilities_justification:
URL: https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#3-roles-and-responsibilities

GOVERNANCE.md §3 documents three roles: Maintainer (design/merge authority for all maintainers, with release authority and the credential trust-root held by the lead maintainer; a lead maintainer plus two co-maintainers, each named with email), Reviewer (anyone listed in .github/CODEOWNERS), and Contributor (anyone opening a PR). Each role lists explicit authorities and responsibilities.
access_continuity_justification:
URL: https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#6-continuity-of-access

GOVERNANCE.md §6 enumerates every credential surface (GitHub org admin, crates.io owners, ghcr.io maintainers, Sigstore signing identity, Pages/DNS) with holder and recovery path. §6.1 names a designated secondary contact with read-only credential-inventory access and Code-of-Conduct escalation authority. §6.2 documents the maintainer-unavailable procedure including GitHub inactive-account recovery.
documentation_roadmap_justification:
URL: https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/blob/main/ROADMAP.md

ROADMAP.md publishes direction at three horizons (near 0-3 months, mid 3-12 months, long 12+ months) covering OpenSSF gap closure, transport-crate extraction, peer-listener hardening (#481), Gold-tier criteria, additional consensus backends, and a public conformance suite.
documentation_architecture_justification:
URL: https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/blob/main/docs/architecture-deep-dive.md

docs/architecture-deep-dive.md documents the project's architecture, complemented by docs/consensus-integration.md (the ConsensusDriver trait), docs/the-allocator.md (the timestamp allocator), docs/operations.md, docs/performance-critical-path.md, docs/key-subsystems.md, and the driver comparison at docs/driver-comparison.md. The in-crate `docs` modules additionally render the algorithm / consensus / operations chapters on docs.rs alongside the API reference.
documentation_security_justification:
URL: https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/blob/main/docs/operations.md

docs/operations.md documents the production deployment surface including TLS/mTLS for peer and admin transports, the secure-by-default Helm chart guards (HA openraft/paxos render fails closed without TLS unless tls.allowInsecurePeer=true is set), and known security considerations. SECURITY.md describes the reporting process and response commitments. The Helm chart documents tls.allowInsecurePeer=true as the operator opt-out (deploy/charts/tsoracle/).
documentation_quick_start_justification:
URL: https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md

docs/getting-started.md provides a quick-start guide. The README at the repository root additionally links to it and to docs/README.md (the documentation table of contents).
documentation_current_justification: Documentation is updated alongside code changes in the same PR. CONTRIBUTING.md (Documentation section) describes the dual-tree layout (root docs/ + in-crate docs modules) and the rule that protocol-visible or allocator changes must update both. release-plz publishes documentation alongside each per-crate release to docs.rs. The pages.yml workflow rebuilds the marketing/documentation site on every push to main.
documentation_achievements_justification:
URL: https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/blob/main/README.md

The README header includes the OpenSSF Best Practices badge (https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/12991) and the OpenSSF Scorecard badge (https://scorecard.dev/viewer/?uri=github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle), both linking to the project's pages on the respective sites and reflecting current achievement status.
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: The project ships a Rust gRPC service, a CLI binary, and library crates; it does not expose graphical user interfaces requiring accessibility (WCAG) compliance. The marketing site at https://www.tsoracle.rs is plain HTML/Markdown documentation.
internationalization_justification: The project's user-facing surface consists of a gRPC API (binary protocol), a CLI binary, structured log lines, and documentation, all in English. It does not contain UI strings or other translatable user-facing content.
sites_password_security_justification: The project does not operate any authentication-requiring website. The marketing site at https://www.tsoracle.rs is static documentation, served over HTTPS. The GitHub repository delegates authentication to GitHub.
maintenance_or_update_justification: The project is actively maintained. Commit cadence on the main branch is multiple commits per week (see https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/commits/main). Dependabot runs weekly across the GitHub Actions, fuzz Cargo, and Docker base-image ecosystems. release-plz publishes per-crate releases on every feat/fix/perf merge to main, with the most recent at https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/releases (multiple releases per week).
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio:
URL: https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/blob/main/SECURITY.md

SECURITY.md commits to crediting reporters in the published advisory unless they request anonymity. The 'Our commitments' section reads: 'Reporters are credited in the advisory unless they request anonymity.'
vulnerability_response_process_justifica:
URL: https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/blob/main/SECURITY.md

`SECURITY.md` documents the full response: 24h ack, 72h triage with severity + preliminary plan, 30d coordinated disclosure (sooner on fix), GitHub-CNA CVE when warranted, reporter credit by default, extension path with operator-visible communication if more time is needed. Scope explicit — in-scope: server binary, client crate, toolkit/driver crates, Helm chart, container images; out-of-scope: upstream-tracked deps, unbounded-resource DoS, attacks requiring root/physical access.
coding_standards_justification:
URL: https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

`CONTRIBUTING.md` documents coding standards: rustfmt formatting; Clippy lint policy with `-D warnings`; the `unwrap_used` / `expect_used` policy for non-test code; performance-critical-path hot-file rules (`scripts/check-critical-path.sh`); canonical Apache-2.0 short license header (`scripts/check-ts-header.py`); Conventional Commits; proto-file expectations (`buf lint` / `format` / `breaking`).
coding_standards_enforced_justification: All coding standards are enforced as required CI checks (.github/workflows/ci.yml): fmt, clippy with -D warnings, deny, header-check, critical-path, buf (lint/format/breaking on PRs). The pre-commit hook at .husky/pre-commit runs fmt and clippy locally before commit. husky-rs auto-installs the hook on the first cargo invocation in any clone (no manual setup required).
build_standard_variables_justification: This is a Rust/Cargo project. Cargo does not consume the GNU-style CC / CFLAGS / CXX / LDFLAGS standard variables that this criterion is written against; it has its own environment variables (RUSTFLAGS, CARGO_TARGET_DIR, CARGO_HOME, etc.) which the project honors via cargo's defaults. The criterion is targeted at GNU autotools / make-style builds.
build_preserve_debug_justification: The release profile in Cargo.toml is `[profile.release] lto = 'thin' codegen-units = 1`, which preserves the symbol information needed for stack traces and crash forensics. Debug info is explicitly preserved at level 2 with packed split-debuginfo for the benchmarks/stress crate (`[profile.release.package.bench-minimal]`). For runtime builds, an operator can re-enable full debug info via RUSTFLAGS without touching project sources.
build_non_recursive_justification: Cargo's workspace build is not recursive in the GNU make sense; cargo computes a single dependency graph from the root Cargo.toml workspace declaration and builds in parallel from one root invocation. The Makefile at the repository root is a thin convenience layer over cargo invocations, not a recursive Makefile.
build_repeatable_justification: The build is repeatable from a clean checkout: `cargo build --workspace --all-features --locked`. The `--locked` flag is mandatory in CI and ensures Cargo.lock is honored exactly. The Rust toolchain is pinned via rust-toolchain.toml. The fuzz workspace has its own pinned Cargo.lock (verified by the fuzz-lockfile CI job) and rust-toolchain.toml pinning nightly. Docker base images are pinned by SHA256 digest in deploy/Dockerfile and refreshed by Dependabot. The deny.toml file pins the cargo-deny advisory-database fetch behavior.
installation_common_justification: The project is installed in idiomatic Rust ways: (1) `cargo install tsoracle` (from crates.io) for the CLI binary; (2) `cargo add tsoracle-client` (etc.) for the library crates; (3) the deploy/Dockerfile + Helm chart at deploy/charts/tsoracle/ for containerized deployment; (4) pre-built images at ghcr.io/prisma-risk/tsoracle-*. The CONTRIBUTING.md `Setup` section enumerates the required system dependencies (protoc, libclang) with platform-specific install commands for macOS and Debian/Ubuntu.
installation_standard_variables_justific: Same as build_standard_variables: this Rust/Cargo project does not consume GNU-style PREFIX/DESTDIR variables. The cargo binary install location is controlled by CARGO_INSTALL_ROOT or standard cargo conventions; the criterion is targeted at GNU autotools / make-style installs.
installation_development_quick_justifica: `cargo build --workspace --all-features` and `cargo test --workspace --all-features` from a clean clone is sufficient to bootstrap a development environment. The required system dependencies (protoc, libclang) are documented at the top of CONTRIBUTING.md with macOS, Debian/Ubuntu install commands matching CI. The pre-commit hook auto-installs on the first cargo invocation, so the developer does not need to run a separate setup script.
external_dependencies_justification:
URL: https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/blob/main/Cargo.lock

External Rust deps live in each crate's `Cargo.toml` `[dependencies]`, with a unified workspace pin in root `[workspace.dependencies]`. Resolved tree pinned in `Cargo.lock`; `fuzz/Cargo.lock` pins the fuzz harness tree. Container base images SHA256-pinned in `deploy/Dockerfile`. CI runs `cargo build/test --locked`; the fuzz-lockfile job forbids `fuzz/Cargo.lock` drift.
dependency_monitoring_justification: Dependabot is configured (.github/dependabot.yml) to update the GitHub Actions ecosystem weekly, the fuzz Cargo workspace weekly, and the Docker base image SHA256 digest pins. cargo-deny check runs in CI against the RustSec advisory database on every PR and every push to main. OpenSSF Scorecard analyzes supply-chain hygiene (.github/workflows/scorecard.yml) on every push and a weekly cron.
updateable_reused_components_justificati: Reused components are kept current via the dependency-monitoring stack (Dependabot + cargo-deny + Scorecard, see dependency_monitoring). The [workspace.dependencies] section in the root Cargo.toml allows centralized pin updates across all 17 workspace crates. release-plz can ship the updated dependency tree to crates.io with per-crate SemVer.
interfaces_current_justification: Public interfaces are documented in docs/interface-reference.md and in the in-crate docs modules (tsoracle_server::docs, tsoracle_core::docs::algorithm, tsoracle_consensus::docs::consensus_integration) which render on docs.rs alongside the API reference. The proto contracts use `buf breaking` (CI job in ci.yml) to detect breaking changes on every PR against the main baseline, so any wire-format change is visible in review.
automated_integration_testing_justificat: Integration tests run automatically in CI on every PR and main-branch push. ~30 in-process integration tests under `crates/*/tests/` (monotonicity, single_node, three_node, snapshot_transfer, restart_replay, reconfiguration, dynamic_membership, etc.). Out-of-process: the kube-e2e lane (`.github/workflows/kube-e2e.yml`, kind cluster, cold-start + rolling-restart soak), mixed-version-soak, stress-smoke (mem/raft/paxos/process topologies with a positive-control inject-violation step), and nightly stress / fuzz / leak runs.
regression_tests_added50_justification: Regression tests are routinely added with bug fixes. Recent examples visible in commit history include test additions for ride-out signal precedence, barrier-seq durable seed, snapshot publish TOCTOU, WatchGuard drop sync stepdown, shutdown stall on hung driver, paxos lease generation wrap, openraft peer RPC deadline, paxos stress scheme-bearing hint, client absolute redirect cap, and openraft meta fuzz decoding. CI's required test step prevents fixes from landing without tests at the architectural level the change touched.
test_statement_coverage80_justification: The project's measured line coverage is approximately 95% via cargo-llvm-cov in the `coverage` CI job, uploaded to Coveralls at https://coveralls.io/github/prisma-risk/tsoracle. This well exceeds the silver-level 80% statement-coverage threshold.
test_policy_mandated_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's `## Test policy` section uses MUST language for both new functionality and bug fixes (see test_policy at passing tier for the URL and full text). The mandate is reinforced by a measured coverage floor (cargo-llvm-cov → Coveralls, currently ~95%); a PR that drops coverage materially without justification will not be merged. Exemptions are limited to commits that do not change runtime behavior (`docs:`, `refactor:`, `chore:`).
implement_secure_design_justification: The implementation reflects the secure-design principles documented in `know_secure_design`: TLS/mTLS with secure-default Helm chart render guard; fail-closed defaults on the consensus/timestamp critical path (single-active stream lease, synchronous step-down at drop, openraft graceful handoff); client-side defense-in-depth (per-pass + absolute redirect caps); decode-boundary input validation backed by 15+ libFuzzer harnesses; non-root pods with NetworkPolicy ingress restriction.
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: Cryptography is delegated to rustls, which supports algorithm agility via its provider abstraction (ring or aws-lc-rs) and its cipher-suite preferences. The PeerTlsConfig and ClientTlsConfig structs accept operator-supplied certificates and CA roots, so an operator can rotate algorithms by issuing certificates with a different signature algorithm and reloading the configuration.
crypto_credential_agility_justification: Operators can rotate TLS credentials without recompiling: PeerTlsConfig and the equivalent client config accept certificate and key paths at process start. In Kubernetes deployments, credentials are mounted from Secrets, which can be rotated via standard Kubernetes Secret rotation.
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: The project verifies peer certificates via rustls's RootCertStore. mTLS configurations require a CA root supplied by the operator (PeerTlsConfig::ca_cert, ClientTlsConfig::ca_cert), and rustls performs full chain validation including hostname (SAN/CN) match. Plaintext fallback is rejected at the Helm chart layer unless explicitly opted in via tls.allowInsecurePeer.
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: TLS private keys are not transmitted by the project itself. Operators supply private keys via filesystem paths (in Kubernetes deployment, via mounted Secret volumes), which are kept out of the repository — no .pem private keys are committed; the only test-cert material is generated at runtime by the rcgen crate during integration tests.
signed_releases_justification:
URL: https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/blob/main/docs/release-signatures.md

Every per-crate GitHub Release is signed via SLSA v1.0 build provenance (`.intoto.jsonl`) generated by `slsa-framework/slsa-github-generator` and signed transparently through Sigstore (Fulcio + Rekor) — no long-lived signing key. End-to-end verification with `slsa-verifier verify-artifact` is documented in `docs/release-signatures.md`, anchored in the Sigstore transparency log. Scope: source crate tarballs; container images at ghcr.io are SHA256-pinned but not yet cosign-signed (follow-up).
version_tags_signed_justification:
URL: https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/blob/main/docs/release-signatures.md#verifying-release-tags

Release tags are annotated and signed via Sigstore gitsign (keyless, transparency-log anchored) in .github/workflows/release-plz.yml. Signing identity = the workflow's GitHub Actions OIDC token, attested by Fulcio, logged to Rekor — same trust model as the SLSA build provenance. Verify: `git verify-tag --raw <tag>` resolves the Fulcio certificate and Rekor entry.
input_validation_justification: The external input surface is the gRPC API; the protobuf-generated decoder is the first validation layer (type-checked, length-prefixed). Above that: barrier-seq invariants in the timestamp allocator; leader-epoch monotonicity checks at the consensus layer; schema-version codecs that fail loud on out-of-range versions (NotRepresentable); and 15+ libFuzzer harnesses (fuzz/fuzz_targets/) exercising decode and roundtrip paths against malformed input across record/openraft/paxos/proto/snapshot/toolkit codecs.
assurance_case_justification:
URL: https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md

`docs/assurance-case.md` presents safety and security claims as a claims → arguments → evidence tree: (1) strict timestamp monotonicity under crashes / partitions / leader handoff / rolling restarts / mixed-version operation, backed by integration tests, kube-e2e soak with measured error budget, stress with positive-control, failpoint/yieldpoint injection, decoder fuzzing; (2) no unauthenticated peer/admin RPCs in the secure-by-default deployment, with one open gap (#481) tracked transparently.
test_invocation_justification:
URL: https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

The project's tests are invoked with `cargo test --workspace --all-features` (documented under 'Running the checks locally' in CONTRIBUTING.md). The Makefile additionally provides convenience targets such as `make test-failpoints` and `make coverage`.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio:
URL: https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml

CI runs on every push to main and every PR via `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Jobs: test (full workspace), cross-platform driver-file (ubuntu/macOS/Windows), buf (proto lint/format/breaking), deny, critical-path, header-check, fuzz-lockfile, coverage, stress-smoke. Other workflows trigger on schedule or paths: fuzz (PR + nightly), kube-e2e + mixed-version-soak, leak/stress nightlies, scorecard, release-plz, release-images, pages.
dynamic_analysis_justification: Multiple dynamic-analysis modes: (1) 15+ libFuzzer harnesses in `fuzz/fuzz_targets/` per-PR (`.github/workflows/fuzz-pr.yml`) and nightly (`.github/workflows/fuzz-nightly.yml`) with auto-issue filing on crash; (2) Kubernetes e2e real-cluster lanes (`kube-e2e.yml`, mixed-version-soak); (3) stress lanes with monotonicity assertion and positive-control `inject-violation` step (`stress-smoke`, `stress-nightly.yml`); (4) `leak-nightly.yml` for memory leaks; (5) failpoint and yieldpoint scaffolding for software-fault injection during integration runs.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: Rust's `debug_assert!` macros are active in debug builds (default for `cargo test`) and in stress-smoke, kube-e2e, and fuzz harness binaries (libFuzzer builds in debug). The project uses `debug_assert!` liberally on invariant-protection paths (e.g., the openraft LeaderState contract guard at run_leader_watch, the PaxosRunner start guard, the consensus barrier-seq invariants).
bus_factor_justification: Three active maintainers as of 2026-05-28: lead maintainer Sebastian Thiebaud plus co-maintainers Charles Merill and Idriss Maoui (`GOVERNANCE.md` §3.1). All hold design and merge authority; the lead maintainer additionally holds release authority and is the credential trust root. Release continuity does not depend on any single person — `GOVERNANCE.md` §6 documents every credential surface with a holder and a recovery path, and the designated secondary contact holds break-glass access to the crates.io owner role and the ghcr.io push credentials. With more than one active maintainer reviewing PRs and able to keep the project moving, the bus factor exceeds one.
crypto_used_network_justification: When transmitting data over networks where confidentiality and integrity are required (peer-to-peer consensus traffic, admin RPCs, client traffic), the project uses TLS or mTLS via rustls. The standalone deployment additionally rejects plaintext peer transport at the Helm chart layer unless explicitly opted in via tls.allowInsecurePeer (see deploy/charts/tsoracle/).
crypto_tls12_justification:
URL: https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/blob/main/docs/operations.md

The project uses TLS 1.3 by default via rustls (rustls's default ClientConfig and ServerConfig). This exceeds the criterion's TLS 1.2 minimum requirement. The rustls default profile additionally rejects TLS 1.0/1.1 entirely.
hardening_justification:
URL: https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/blob/main/docs/operations.md

Hardening mechanisms: (1) safe Rust structurally excludes memory-safety vulnerability classes; (2) deployed pods run non-root (`fsGroup: 10001` for EBS-mounted volumes); (3) container base images are SHA256-pinned and refreshed by Dependabot; (4) the Helm chart applies NetworkPolicies restricting Ingress to expected sources; (5) Clippy `-D warnings` plus `unwrap_used` / `expect_used` lints fail any panicking call in non-test code at CI time.
contributors_unassociated_justification:
URL: https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/graphs/contributors

As of 2026-05-26 contributors are not yet from organizations unassociated with the primary maintainer. Early-stage; outside contributions have not yet broadened the base. Path to Met (ROADMAP.md): publish ROADMAP.md on the documentation site, maintain `good first issue` / `help wanted` triage in CONTRIBUTING.md's 'Where to start', and link from adjacent Rust-ecosystem consensus / distributed-systems forums.
copyright_per_file_justification: Every first-party .rs file in the project carries the canonical short license header containing `SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0` and the project's copyright statement. The header format is enforced by `scripts/check-ts-header.py` in CI on every PR (the `header-check` job in .github/workflows/ci.yml). The canonical header text lives at scripts/header.txt; the full Apache-2.0 license text and copyright is at LICENSE.
license_per_file_justification: Every first-party .rs file carries `SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0` in its canonical short header, enforced by scripts/check-ts-header.py in CI.
small_tasks_justification:
URL: https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#where-to-start

`CONTRIBUTING.md` 'Where to start' points first-time contributors at the `good first issue` and `help wanted` label searches on the issue tracker, plus three concrete starter areas (documentation polish, additional fuzz targets, additional integration tests). Open issues are triaged and labeled.
code_review_standards_justification:
URL: https://github.com/prisma-risk/tsoracle/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

CONTRIBUTING.md documents the project's review and contribution process (required CI checks, coding standards, proto/buf expectations, Conventional Commits, rebase-and-squash flow). Branch protection on main requires PR review before merge. The .github/CODEOWNERS file assigns code-owner review responsibility. The required CI checks (test, clippy with -D warnings, deny, buf, header-check, critical-path) must pass before merge.
two_person_review_justification: Branch protection on `main` requires at least one approving review from a person other than the author before merge; a maintainer cannot self-merge their own PR, and this applies to maintainers' own changes (no admin bypass for merges). With multiple active maintainers (GOVERNANCE.md §3.1), every proposed modification — including a maintainer's own PRs — is reviewed by a non-author, so well above 50% of modifications are reviewed by someone other than the author. The required-checks list (test, clippy with -D warnings, deny, buf, header-check, critical-path) must also pass before merge.
build_reproducible_justification: The build is repeatable (build_repeatable, silver) but not bit-for-bit reproducible across hosts. Rust does not currently guarantee bit-for-bit reproducible release-profile builds across different build hosts (timestamps embedded in linker metadata vary by build environment and linker version). The project has not invested in the reproducible-build tooling (e.g., diffoscope-driven CI gate) required to overcome this. Action: add a reproducible-build CI lane if/when stable Rust reaches deterministic release builds.
test_statement_coverage90_justification: The project's measured line coverage is approximately 95% via cargo-llvm-cov in the `coverage` CI job (Coveralls at https://coveralls.io/github/prisma-risk/tsoracle). This exceeds the gold-level 90% statement-coverage threshold.
test_branch_coverage80_justification: Branch coverage is not currently measured separately. cargo-llvm-cov in the `coverage` CI job is configured for line coverage (~95%); branch coverage requires the `--branch` flag and a separate report consumer. Action: enable branch coverage in `make coverage`, then assess whether it meets the gold 80% threshold.
security_review_justification: A formal third-party security review has not been conducted on the project. The project has had multiple finding-driven incremental improvements via the issue tracker and security PRs (e.g., the Helm peer-mTLS-default fix, the peer-listener-secure-by-default work, the client absolute redirect cap, the paxos lease generation wrap fix), and security findings are tracked via OpenSSF Scorecard and cargo-deny, but no comprehensive external review. Action: commission a third-party security review ahead of the 1.0 release.
